microscopic_coupling_only.caveat: This baseline uses the screened solar charge with surface compactness only. It yields 3.2e-29 (~10⁻²⁹), confirming that the measured η is not produced by the microscopic coupling alone. η is an emergent observable response coefficient.

standard_scalar_tensor.caveat: Standard scalar-tensor Nordtvedt formula. The ~13.7× enhancement (using the Cassini upper-bound α_0 ≲ 3×10⁻³) indicates that η absorbs additional contributions from the TEP screening mechanism beyond bare scalar-tensor physics.

volumetric_tep.caveat: Effective observable-response band from integrated density profiles (step_026), not a decomposable force estimate — see the product-limit check below. Superseded by the canonical pairwise operator (Paper 0 v0.15, Appendix E R11).

source_charge_product_limit.verdict: A mediated differential-fall signature is product-limited by both vertices: δa/a_0 = (α_0 S_Σ^(⊙))·Δα_body ≲ 10⁻⁹–10⁻⁸, five orders below the measured band. The volumetric estimate therefore cannot be a charge×charge force estimate; as a full-response coefficient it is not independent of the source charge it must contain.

cmb_orientation_prediction.formula: η_θ ≈ η₀ m_CMB from eq:cmb_anisotropy; |m_CMB| ~ O(1) ⇒ |η_θ| ~ |η₀|

order_of_magnitude_band.note: Same response-coefficient decade as pooled synodic η (Step 033).

conclusion: η = -3.1773e-04 is the LLR observable response coefficient. The baselines adjudicate which sectors can carry it: (1) screened-charge compactness-squared η = (α_0 S_Σ)² Δ(Φ²) = 3.2464e-29 yields an enhancement of 9.79e+24×, confirming that η is emergent and not produced by the screened solar source charge alone; (2) standard scalar-tensor η = 2α_0²/(1+α_0²) = 2.3120e-05 yields an enhancement of 13.7×, indicating that η absorbs TEP-specific screening contributions beyond standard scalar-tensor physics; (3) the volumetric model η ≈ α_eff^(⊕-Moon) Δ⟨(ρ/ρ_T)³⟩ = -9.6594e-05 is an effective response band, not a decomposable force estimate — the source-charge product limit returns -7.92e-10 with the shielding differential (-2.46e-08 treating α_eff as the full body differential), five orders below the measured band, and the canonical pairwise operator independently suppresses the Earth–Moon force channel to ~10⁻¹⁴. The admissible sector is the clock-sector/ephemeris-reduction projection, whose amplitude map is the open estimand question of the source-level integrator refit. The measured η is much smaller than cross-domain κ values (η/κ_Cep ~ -3.03e-10), consistent with LLR being in a more screened Solar System regime.
